name: MD-07
label: Safe D

key_factors: District leans about 31 points Democratic, one of the bluest House seats
Incumbent Mfume holds a large cash edge while challenger Collier shows no reported fundraising
Prediction markets price Democratic win odds near 96 percent
No public polls or expert ratings; forecast rests on district fundamentals
model.rationale: The seat's 31-point Democratic lean, Mfume's financial advantage, and a challenger with no visible fundraising operation leave almost no path for an upset, and markets and fundamentals point the same direction. With no polling available, uncertainty stays wide, but not nearly wide enough to threaten the incumbent.
model.watch: Only an extraordinary development, such as a major scandal or a suddenly well-funded challenger campaign, would put this seat in any genuine doubt.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Maryland's 7th District sits about 31 points on the Democratic side in partisan lean, making it one of the most heavily Democratic seats on the House map. Kweisi Mfume, the Democratic incumbent, is running for re-election and holds a clear financial edge, with roughly $700,000 in cash on hand after raising about $415,000.

Republican Scott Collier has reported no fundraising in the available data, and no public polls or expert ratings follow the race. Prediction markets price Democratic chances at about 96 percent. With the district's strong lean, the incumbent's resources, and the challenger's minimal visible campaign, the realistic question is the size of the Democratic margin rather than which party wins the seat.
